The recovery fence described in "},{"type":"text","text":"Consistency and recovery","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"/teams/07f8fd73-cdf4-516a-91ed-41cee8e97b70/p/19a0c982-2c1a-56a3-9536-556f77f40acb/docs/57bf4c8b-ccf8-5b08-9020-0c6ddb60b666","target":"_self","rel":"noopener noreferrer"}}]},{"type":"text","text":" protects against resuming with a mixed state after an interrupted restore."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Search and optional services"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Keyword search is available without a successful embedding request. Semantic search depends on compatible embeddings and pgvector data. AI writing uses configured providers. Office previews run through the preview service; HTML export and attachment download have their own paths. See the subsystem reference pages before promising availability in a specific deployment."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Deployment boundary"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The repository's Docker Compose setup is the concrete deployment asset. Kubernetes and Azure architecture documents are reference material. Current container builds run in CI and publish images; operators deploy a selected image revision. Application schema migrations must remain immutable after deployment."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Source: examples/kollab-team/pages/architecture.md"}]}]}

Installation-specific cluster records and replication identity do not travel in the archive."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"File restore stages incoming uploads and retains previous bytes until the database step succeeds. PostgreSQL and the filesystem cannot commit as one native transaction. If interruption leaves a recovery directory, the application blocks further workspace operations until an administrator reconciles the outcome."}]},{"type":"macroBlock","attrs":{"type":"mermaid","config":{"code":"---

  DB -->|Failure| Rollback[Roll back staged files]
  Rollback -->|Recovery incomplete| Fence[Block workspace until reconciled]","theme":"auto"}}},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Air-gap exchange"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Sync ZIPs use "},{"type":"text","text":"kollab.sync.v3","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":", with operations, uploaded files, and a signature. Trusted installations share a signing key of at least 32 bytes. Vector clocks distinguish later versions from concurrent changes; tombstones prevent older packages from resurrecting deleted records. A complete sync merges the source state and preserves unrelated destination data."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Use cursor zero for a complete exchange. Incremental cursors belong to a source/destination direction and advance only after successful import. Do not use this demonstration backup as a sync package; its file format and semantics differ."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Verification evidence"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The repository tests cover database round trips, rollback, signatures, conflict review, and replica state. The showcase adds a real-database archive test that seeds only demonstration data, exports through the production handler, changes the disposable target, restores through the production handler, and compares the resulting data and files. The artifact is therefore validated against the code that users will invoke."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Source: examples/kollab-team/pages/consistency.md"}]}]}

documents.title: Local User Management
documents.content: {"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"macroBlock","attrs":{"type":"page-properties","config":{"properties":[{"key":"Area","value":"Product","type":"text"},{"key":"Audience","value":"Authors and reviewers","type":"text"},{"key":"Availability","value":"Reference; see section status","type":"text"}]}}},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Local user management is Kollab's first-run default: leave "},{"type":"text","text":"AUTH_MODE","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" unset, or set "},{"type":"text","text":"AUTH_MODE=local","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":". It is intended for offline or single-site installations that do not use an OIDC identity provider."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Before the first start, set "},{"type":"text","text":"JWT_SECRET","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" to a unique secret of at least 32 bytes. Open Kollab after it starts and it will prompt you to create the first account. That account is automatically a system administrator."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The first-account prompt is available only while the installation has no users, and it closes permanently after successful creation. Public account registration is not available. Sign in as that administrator, open "},{"type":"text","text":"Server Settings","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":", and select "},{"type":"text","text":"Users","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" in the administration sidebar (or open "},{"type":"text","text":"/_admin/users","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":"). From there you can create accounts, edit display names and email addresses, reset passwords, enable or disable sign-in, and permanently remove an account. Usernames are permanent account IDs. Disabled users cannot sign in, and the signed-in account cannot disable or remove itself. After five failed sign-in attempts for the same username and source address, Kollab pauses further attempts for 15 minutes."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Choose either local accounts or OIDC for a deployment. Moving to OIDC later should be planned as an identity migration, using the provider's stable subject identifier for administrator bootstrap."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Attachments and previews follow the same page access rules as their parent document. Links copied from the browser only work for an authenticated user who can read that document."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Source: user_guide/local_user_management.md"}]}]}

documents.title: OpenID Connect Single Sign-On
documents.content: {"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"macroBlock","attrs":{"type":"page-properties","config":{"properties":[{"key":"Area","value":"Product","type":"text"},{"key":"Audience","value":"Authors and reviewers","type":"text"},{"key":"Availability","value":"Reference; see section status","type":"text"}]}}},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Kollab uses OpenID Connect (OIDC) for production single sign-on. This works with corporate identity platforms and self-hosted identity hubs such as Authentik."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"An administrator must set these server values before starting Kollab:"}]},{"type":"bulletList","content":[{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"OIDC_AUTHORITY","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":": the provider's HTTPS issuer URL."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"OIDC_CLIENT_ID","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":": the Kollab browser application's client ID."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"OIDC_REDIRECT_URI","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":": the exact public URL that users return to after sign-in."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"OIDC_API_AUDIENCE","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":": the identity provider's audience identifier for the Kollab API resource."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"OIDC_API_SCOPE","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":": the delegated scope the browser must request before it can call the Kollab API."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USER_ID","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":": the stable OIDC "},{"type":"text","text":"sub","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" value for the first Kollab administrator."}]}]}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Kollab discovers the provider configuration automatically. After sign-in, the browser receives an ID token and an access token; Kollab sends only the access token to its API. The API verifies the token's issuer, signature, expiry, configured API audience, and delegated API scope. Do not use a client secret in the browser or configure a generic shared JWT secret for OIDC."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"After the first administrator has logged in and other administrators are configured, remove "},{"type":"text","text":"BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USER_ID","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" from the deployment configuration. This avoids keeping an implicit permanent administrator grant in infrastructure."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"For an organisation that requires SAML, configure the identity hub to accept SAML from the corporate provider and issue OIDC to Kollab. This keeps the Kollab integration simple and lets one identity hub serve the rest of the homelab."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Source: user_guide/oidc_sso.md"}]}]}

It contains page content, versions, accounts, permissions, settings, and uploaded files."}]}]}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"An export briefly coordinates activity across API replicas so the database and files are captured consistently. It preserves the local workspace's data; replica presence and installation-specific coordination credentials are excluded."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Restore an archive"}]},{"type":"orderedList","attrs":{"start":1},"content":[{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Ask editors to save their current work."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Open "},{"type":"text","text":"Server Settings → Backup & sync","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" and select "},{"type":"text","text":"Upload & Restore Backup ZIP","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":"."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Choose a complete archive from the same compatible application schema."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Wait for confirmation. Open editors reload to use the restored state."}]}]}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Restore replaces the target installation's application data and files. It is different from "},{"type":"text","text":"synchronization","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"/teams/07f8fd73-cdf4-516a-91ed-41cee8e97b70/p/190f2538-c6f6-5739-a11c-0f6026f6d994/docs/98a1c976-1b34-591a-aa80-173f32e4781e","target":"_self","rel":"noopener noreferrer"}}]},{"type":"text","text":", which merges changes and reviews conflicts. Partial or legacy archives and mismatched migration versions are rejected; no compatibility with old sync formats is provided."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"If validation or the database transaction fails, the existing data is retained and staged files are rolled back. If recovery files are preserved after an interruption or rollback failure, stop retrying and have the server administrator reconcile the recovery directory and database outcome. Workspace operations remain blocked until recovery is complete."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"See "},{"type":"text","text":"deployment and recovery operations"},{"type":"text","text":" and "},{"type":"text","text":"the technical design","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"/teams/07f8fd73-cdf4-516a-91ed-41cee8e97b70/p/19a0c982-2c1a-56a3-9536-556f77f40acb/docs/232d23bb-5467-54e1-bd6c-60590a284935","target":"_self","rel":"noopener noreferrer"}}]},{"type":"text","text":"."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Source: user_guide/backups_and_restores.md"}]}]}

documents.content: {"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"macroBlock","attrs":{"type":"page-properties","config":{"properties":[{"key":"Area","value":"Product","type":"text"},{"key":"Audience","value":"Authors and reviewers","type":"text"},{"key":"Availability","value":"Reference; see section status","type":"text"}]}}},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Server administrators can exchange changes in both directions between separate Kollab installations. Open "},{"type":"text","text":"Server settings → Backup & sync → Bidirectional Air-Gap Sync","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":". Azure backup and Jira remain prototypes."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Before the first exchange, configure the same private "},{"type":"text","text":"SYNC_SIGNING_KEY","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" on both installations and run the same application version. The key must be at least 32 bytes long. A sync ZIP includes sensitive workspace and account data; exchange it only with trusted administrators. Old sync ZIP formats are not supported. Create fresh packages with this version."}]},{"type":"orderedList","attrs":{"start":1},"content":[{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"On the source installation, leave "},{"type":"text","text":"Since Operation ID","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" at "},{"type":"text","text":"0","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" and select "},{"type":"text","text":"Export Sync ZIP","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":". This includes its complete tracked state and uploaded files."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"On the destination, select "},{"type":"text","text":"Import Sync ZIP","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" and choose that file."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"If a conflict appears, compare "},{"type":"text","text":"This installation","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" with "},{"type":"text","text":"Incoming installation","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":". Select "},{"type":"text","text":"Keep this installation’s version","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":", "},{"type":"text","text":"Use incoming version","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":", or "},{"type":"text","text":"Cancel import","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":". Each decision applies only to the displayed conflict. Additional conflicts appear separately."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Wait for the successful import message. Until every conflict is resolved, the import leaves the destination unchanged."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Export from the destination and import back into the original source to carry its changes and your resolutions in the reverse direction."}]}]}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Duplicate packages and older versions of records are safe to import again. Deleted records stay deleted when an older package arrives. A full sync merges changes and preserves unrelated destination data; a full backup restore replaces data."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"For small workspaces, using "},{"type":"text","text":"0","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" for each exchange is the easiest workflow. Advanced users can find the greatest operation "},{"type":"text","text":"id","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" in "},{"type":"text","text":"sync_operations.json","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" inside an exported ZIP and use it as the next cursor after successful import. Track cursors separately for each direction and destination. Never reuse another installation's cursor or advance one after a failed import."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Page moves or deletions can conflict with work that exists only on the destination. If the message identifies dependent records or incompatible page locations, move or reconcile those pages in the workspace before importing again. Conflicts select an entire record; inspect related page-content conflicts carefully. Both resolved database versions remain in the server's synchronization audit records. Losing file versions remain in local recovery storage for an administrator to retrieve."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":1},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Working across API replicas"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"An installation can run multiple API processes while everyone uses the same workspace address. The supplied Docker Compose setup defaults to two. Edits, online presence, and cursor positions cross process boundaries. Reconnecting through another process retrieves accepted changes from the shared database. The verified concurrency target is 2–5 editors."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"If the collaboration connection is unavailable, keep the page open. Editing waits for initial synchronization. After a page version restore or administrative import, open pages reload to use the authoritative restored data. Save current work before those operations."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"For deployment, all API processes must use the same database, sign-in configuration, and writable uploads directory. Administrators can set "},{"type":"text","text":"API_REPLICAS","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" to change the number of processes. Separate uploads folders on each process are not supported."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"If an interrupted archive operation reports that recovery is required, further workspace operations pause to protect its data. Have the server administrator inspect the preserved recovery directory and database outcome before resuming. Ordinary sync conflicts only require the review controls above."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"See "},{"type":"text","text":"technical implementation and recovery details","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"/teams/07f8fd73-cdf4-516a-91ed-41cee8e97b70/p/19a0c982-2c1a-56a3-9536-556f77f40acb/docs/232d23bb-5467-54e1-bd6c-60590a284935","target":"_self","rel":"noopener noreferrer"}}]},{"type":"text","text":" and "},{"type":"text","text":"verification results","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"/teams/07f8fd73-cdf4-516a-91ed-41cee8e97b70/p/19a0c982-2c1a-56a3-9536-556f77f40acb/docs/0dabf569-5ac4-5fd5-99ce-e4f0f2447907","target":"_self","rel":"noopener noreferrer"}}]},{"type":"text","text":"."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Deployment uses the exact verified Git revision without changing package versions on the server. The deployment checks every API replica before reporting success. Generated browser test output is excluded from source control."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The edge proxy defaults to host ports 80 and 443; "},{"type":"text","text":"HTTP_PORT","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" and "},{"type":"text","text":"HTTPS_PORT","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" can override them. Existing additional proxy sites are preserved. Deployment initializes a missing sync signing key privately in the server environment file. Use the same key on trusted peer installations before exchanging sync packages."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Source: user_guide/synchronization.md"}]}]}

descendant's "},{"type":"text","text":"TeamID","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" and "},{"type":"text","text":"ProjectID","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":". This avoids relying on the old space's listing filter, which intentionally hides project pages from a team-root listing."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Root and personal moves","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":": Omitting destination IDs only re-parents a page at the root of its current space, preserving backward-compatible API behavior. Moving to Personal Space supplies the explicit "},{"type":"text","text":"personal_","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" team ID, clears "},{"type":"text","text":"projectId","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":", and propagates that location through the branch."}]}]}]},{"type":"horizontalRule"},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"7. Automated System Backups"}]},{"type":"calloutPanel","attrs":{"type":"note","title":"NOTE"},"content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Status:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" ⚪ Planned"}]}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"To ensure disaster recovery, Kollab utilizes the same Go cron worker system to manage automated database snapshots."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"7.1 Backup Routine"}]},{"type":"orderedList","attrs":{"start":1},"content":[{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Trigger","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":": A nightly (or weekly) cron job fires."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Snapshot","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":": The worker executes a "},{"type":"text","text":"pg_dump","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" of the entire PostgreSQL database schema and data."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Compression","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":": The resulting SQL file is compressed (gzip)."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Upload","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":": The compressed payload is uploaded securely to the currently configured storage backend (e.g., S3 or Azure Blob Storage)."}]}]}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":3},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"7.2 Retention Policy"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Administrators can define a backup retention policy (e.g., keep the last 7 daily backups and 4 weekly backups). The cron worker will automatically prune old backups from the storage provider after a successful new upload."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Source: design/05_data_lifecycle.md"}]}]}

See "},{"type":"text","text":"Caddy's dynamic upstream specification","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/reverse_proxy#dynamic-upstreams","target":"_blank","rel":"noopener noreferrer"}}]},{"type":"text","text":"."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"0014_cluster.sql","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" creates "},{"type":"text","text":"cluster_control","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" (epoch, tree revision, media signing key) and transient "},{"type":"text","text":"cluster_presence","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" rows. These records and credentials never cross installations in backups or sync packages. Page media capability signatures work across API replicas and process restarts because their signing key is stored in this installation's database."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"ws.Hub.RunContext","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" polls PostgreSQL every 250 ms for active rooms. Full Yjs snapshots remain authoritative in "},{"type":"text","text":"collaborative_states","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":"; the accepted version and readable projection are committed by compare-and-swap. A stale writer receives the accepted state and merges it in the browser before retrying. Presence uses per-connection UUIDs and expires after 15 seconds; cursor positions are shared with the presence heartbeat. Polling errors leave accepted state intact. No Redis or sticky-session requirement is introduced."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The browser disables editing until initial synchronization completes. The first editor must receive its initialization acknowledgement. A losing initializer reloads before merging duplicated JSON seeds, including viewers that rendered a local initial copy. Reconnect keeps ordinary unsent edits, but a changed restoration epoch causes reload before old CRDT state can enter a restored document."}]},{"type":"macroBlock","attrs":{"type":"mermaid","config":{"code":"---

Ordinary HTTP work and WebSocket state operations take shared locks; archive exports/imports, version restore, end-of-session checkpoints, and cleanup use the appropriate exclusive gate. A separate connection pool serves distributed locks so waiting requests cannot exhaust connections needed by the lock holder. Startup initialization is serialized with a dedicated PostgreSQL connection."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Backup restore, sync import, and page version restore advance "},{"type":"text","text":"cluster_control.epoch","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" in the same database transaction as the authoritative change. Every replica invalidates its rooms before processing another edit. Local disconnect signals use WebSocket close code 1012. End-of-session checkpoints check remote presence and serialize their final content comparison."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"File installation stages on the shared uploads mount and rolls back on database failure. A process interruption leaves a "},{"type":"text","text":".kollab-restore-*","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" directory. Startup and subsequent coordinated operations refuse to use the workspace while that recovery marker remains. An operator must reconcile its "},{"type":"text","text":"previous-uploads","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":", staged files, and database outcome before removing it. PostgreSQL plus a filesystem cannot offer a single cross-resource transaction; this fence prevents silent use of a potentially mixed state."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Separate installations exchanging packages"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"0015_bidirectional_sync.sql","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" provides:"}]},{"type":"table","content":[{"type":"tableRow","content":[{"type":"tableHeader","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Table"}]}]},{"type":"tableHeader","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Purpose"}]}]}]},{"type":"tableRow","content":[{"type":"tableCell","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"replication_identity","marks":[{"type":"code"}]}]}]},{"type":"tableCell","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Local installation UUID; excluded from archives and renewed after restore"}]}]}]},{"type":"tableRow","content":[{"type":"tableCell","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"replication_records","marks":[{"type":"code"}]}]}]},{"type":"tableCell","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Latest full row/tombstone and vector clock per portable row key"}]}]}]},{"type":"tableRow","content":[{"type":"tableCell","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"replication_events","marks":[{"type":"code"}]}]}]},{"type":"tableCell","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"One compact latest event per row, with a monotonically advancing local export cursor"}]}]}]},{"type":"tableRow","content":[{"type":"tableCell","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"replication_conflicts","marks":[{"type":"code"}]}]}]},{"type":"tableCell","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Both database versions and the administrator's committed resolution"}]}]}]}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Tracking is enabled after permission-schema setup for every primary-key application table. Internal replication, cluster, migration, and obsolete operation-log tables are excluded. No-op updates do not advance clocks. Changing a primary key creates a tombstone for the former identity."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Most rows use their primary key as portable identity. The permissions library uses local serial IDs; "},{"type":"text","text":"principal_roles","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" and "},{"type":"text","text":"permission_grants","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" therefore receive UUID "},{"type":"text","text":"sync_id","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" columns. Assignments derive a stable UUID from principal, role, and binding values; grants receive random UUIDs. Numeric local IDs are omitted from transport and allocated locally, avoiding collisions between independent installations."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"POST /api/system/sync/import","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" and "},{"type":"text","text":"GET /api/system/sync/export?since_id=0","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" require server administration. The signed ZIP contains "},{"type":"text","text":"sync_operations.json","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":", uploaded files, and "},{"type":"text","text":"signature.txt","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":". "},{"type":"text","text":"SYNC_SIGNING_KEY","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" must match between trusted installations and contain at least 32 bytes. Signatures cover ordered entry names, sizes, payloads, and file bytes. A signed package is trusted administrative data, including account/permission changes and service settings."}]},{"type":"codeBlock","attrs":{"language":"json"},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{
  "format": "kollab.sync.v3",
  "operations": [{
    "id": 42,
    "event_id": "a7bbccf1-55e6-4ebe-ab54-41bfdb621069",
    "source_id": "e3b2b65b-9076-49d6-bc7c-1de96f5b728b",
    "table_name": "teams",
    "record_key": "{\"id\": \"team-example\"}",
    "action": "UPDATE",
    "row_data": {"id": "team-example", "name": "Example"},
    "clock": {"e3b2b65b-9076-49d6-bc7c-1de96f5b728b": 3}
  }]
}"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The row example is abbreviated; real events include all transferable columns. Vector clocks distinguish later, earlier/equal, and concurrent changes. Earlier/equal events are ignored, and tombstones prevent resurrection. Concurrent equal data joins its clocks automatically. Other concurrent data returns HTTP 409 with redacted local/incoming previews and a conflict identifier bound to both versions. The whole import rolls back. The frontend sends explicit choices in a multipart "},{"type":"text","text":"resolutions","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" map ("},{"type":"text","text":"keep-local","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" or "},{"type":"text","text":"use-incoming","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":"); each accepted decision joins both clocks and advances the importing node. Reverse exchange propagates that decision. A changed conflict requires another review."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Upserts run in foreign-key order; deletions run in reverse order, including document parent depth. A parent deletion cannot cascade into unmentioned destination-only records. Combined moves must preserve parent/project/team scope and have no ancestry cycles. A dependency or uniqueness conflict is rejected atomically; reconcile that relationship in the workspace before retrying. This is explicit row-level conflict selection, not automatic semantic merging of disconnected page edits."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Same-path files with different hashes also require a decision. Losing bytes are retained under "},{"type":"text","text":"uploads/.kollab-sync-conflicts/<conflict-id>/<sha256>","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" with "},{"type":"text","text":"original-path.txt","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":". This local recovery history is included in full backups but excluded from outgoing sync. Database conflict history is local and included in full backups. Recovery paths cannot be injected by sync packages."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Use cursor 0 for a complete state exchange. For incremental exchange, record the greatest event "},{"type":"text","text":"id","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" in the exported package separately for each source/destination pair, and advance it only after the destination successfully imports. Cursors are local, not interchangeable between installations. Full packages are safe to repeat. They merge the source state; they do not delete unrelated destination data."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Verification"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Integration tests exercise two PostgreSQL installations, independent permission ID allocation, conflicts and reverse propagation, old-package rejection by clock, deletion tombstones, compact cursors, dependent-record protection, shared maintenance locks, media keys, presence expiry, two hubs with five editors, stale writes, surviving-replica reconnect, and restoration epochs. HTTP tests cover file conflict review, database-failure rollback, and preservation of losing file bytes. Frontend tests cover reviewed decisions, cancellation, duplicate-submit prevention, first initialization, and epoch reloads."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"See "},{"type":"text","text":"readiness results","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"/teams/07f8fd73-cdf4-516a-91ed-41cee8e97b70/p/19a0c982-2c1a-56a3-9536-556f77f40acb/docs/0dabf569-5ac4-5fd5-99ce-e4f0f2447907","target":"_self","rel":"noopener noreferrer"}}]},{"type":"text","text":" and "},{"type":"text","text":"administrator instructions","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"/teams/07f8fd73-cdf4-516a-91ed-41cee8e97b70/p/190f2538-c6f6-5739-a11c-0f6026f6d994/docs/98a1c976-1b34-591a-aa80-173f32e4781e","target":"_self","rel":"noopener noreferrer"}}]},{"type":"text","text":"."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The final full backend run passed at "},{"type":"text","text":"63.9% statement coverage","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":". All "},{"type":"text","text":"113 frontend tests","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" passed; the production TypeScript/build checks and targeted race checks passed. The synchronization settings page was inspected in light and dark modes; custom controls use injected theme variables."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Deployment uses the exact verified Git revision without changing package versions on the server. The deployment checks every API replica before reporting success. Generated browser test output is excluded from source control."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The edge proxy defaults to host ports 80 and 443; "},{"type":"text","text":"HTTP_PORT","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" and "},{"type":"text","text":"HTTPS_PORT","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" can override them. Existing additional proxy sites are preserved. Deployment initializes a missing sync signing key privately in the server environment file. Use the same key on trusted peer installations before exchanging sync packages."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Images are built in GitHub Actions and distributed through GHCR. The droplet only downloads and starts the selected images. The local "},{"type":"text","text":"build.sh","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" uses the same Dockerfiles and pinned converter source; see "},{"type":"text","text":"Container releases","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"/teams/07f8fd73-cdf4-516a-91ed-41cee8e97b70/p/19a0c982-2c1a-56a3-9536-556f77f40acb/docs/b4c99bb3-5211-5b70-bb51-ac8e7cc5ebab","target":"_self","rel":"noopener noreferrer"}}]},{"type":"text","text":" for image identity, authentication, failure handling, and local build options."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Source: design/multi_instance_sync.md"}]}]}

config:
  htmlLabels: false

---
sequenceDiagram
  participant Server
  participant DB as PostgreSQL
  Server->>DB: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations
  Server->>Server: Load embedded migrations in version order
  loop each migration
    Server->>DB: Read version and SHA-256 checksum
    alt unapplied
      Server->>DB: BEGIN, execute SQL, record version/checksum, COMMIT
    else applied with matching checksum
      Server->>Server: Skip
    else checksum differs
      Server-->>Server: Fail startup
    end
  end","theme":"auto"}}},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"0001","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" is the existing cumulative schema baseline. The compact-navigation breakpoint is 900 CSS pixels; "},{"type":"text","text":"100dvh","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" and flex minimum sizes account for browser chrome and keep independent scroll regions usable."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Editor"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"EditorCanvas","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" owns the live formatting toolbar. Below 900 pixels it uses "},{"type":"text","text":"flex-wrap: nowrap","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":", a bounded width, horizontal overflow, and non-shrinking controls. The toolbar has a keyboard focus target and an accessible label that describes sideways navigation. Touch controls are at least 44 pixels. Desktop toolbar wrapping is unchanged. Page titles use an autosizing multiline field, retaining the 28/36-pixel title scale and Enter-to-focus-editor behavior. Mobile decorative background glows are omitted because their absolute dimensions previously widened the editor's scrollable area."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"EditorHeader","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" retains primary actions and visible Edit/Done labels on phones. Secondary history, analytics, and watch controls move into the page-actions menu. The menu itself remains available to readers, while its original mutation entries remain disabled unless "},{"type":"text","text":"canEdit","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" is true. Its existing deleted-page restriction remains in place. This does not change server authorization. Desktop secondary controls remain visible."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"CommentDrawer","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" changes from persistent desktop navigation to a temporary mobile drawer. The desktop paper is positioned relative to its flex region instead of using a hard-coded top offset. Mobile paper is capped to the viewport, handles safe-area/classification offsets, and uses MUI backdrop, focus, and Escape behavior."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"DocumentPage","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" supplies no collaboration token to "},{"type":"text","text":"EditorCanvas","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" only when explicitly rendered in mock mode. This enables local component/UI authoring checks without waiting for a nonexistent mock WebSocket server. Authenticated production pages continue to wait for synchronization readiness. Mock UI checks do not replace real multi-replica synchronization tests."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Forms and controls"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The mobile CSS rule raises native and MUI text-entry controls to 16 pixels to avoid automatic zoom on iOS. "},{"type":"text","text":"touch-action: manipulation","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" applies to controls while retaining pinch zoom. "},{"type":"text","text":"TopNavbar","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" uses semantic buttons for the account and home controls, labelled navigation/search controls, and router navigation instead of full-document reloads."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Admin forms use responsive grids and local table-scroll regions. Color styling continues to come from theme variables; the theme chooser intentionally previews each preset's own colors. No mobile stylesheet supplies a separate fixed light/dark palette."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Verification"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Frontend unit tests cover route-based admin/sidebar substitution, keyboard and pointer navigation, focus restoration, mobile search, and pending-save behavior. Bounded browser verification uses mock data to inspect phone, tablet, and desktop widths, route/content overflow, editing controls, and light/dark theme presets. The temporary verification server and entry point are removed afterward."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"See "},{"type":"text","text":"mobile user instructions","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"/teams/07f8fd73-cdf4-516a-91ed-41cee8e97b70/p/190f2538-c6f6-5739-a11c-0f6026f6d994/docs/ac799125-fd3d-50d4-b4f5-2eb20930a3c0","target":"_self","rel":"noopener noreferrer"}}]},{"type":"text","text":"."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Source: design/responsive_authoring.md"}]}]}

Local qualification includes the selected bidirectional sync and multi-instance operating model. External-service checks remain deployment-specific. Azure backup and Jira remain intentional prototypes. Other advertised features are being checked against their implementation and integration paths; passing a bundle build alone is not release qualification."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The baseline review found document collection authorization gaps, WebSocket write authorization gaps, unscoped administrative archive operations, incomplete database restore and sync import, incomplete route wiring, local session propagation failures, and missing release checks. Baseline frontend verification passed 103 tests in 22 files and built a production bundle. The actual TypeScript project check reported 368 diagnostics; the documented root "},{"type":"text","text":"tsc --noEmit","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" checked no application files. Backend integration tests ran against disposable PostgreSQL and failed an authentication configuration expectation. The validation results after fixes are recorded below."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Authorization uses the same document evaluator for lists and direct reads. Slugs and aliases resolve before ancestry evaluation. Versions are confined to their document. Non-document resources use explicit scope checks; administrative backup and sync operations require server administration. WebSocket connections remain bound to the document authorized at connection time, recheck access before delivery and updates, and reject write updates from readers. Local sessions are checked against the current active user and a credential fingerprint so deleting, disabling, or changing the password invalidates old credentials."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Destination validation binds a parent, project, and team to one real space and requires write access before creating or moving content. Personal spaces receive an owner role. HTTP headers have bounded read time, requests have size limits, and request logging redacts browser attachment credentials as well as WebSocket tokens."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"See "},{"type":"text","text":"the user-facing readiness notes"},{"type":"text","text":". This document records the verified scope and remaining release gates."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Implemented boundaries and behavior"}]},{"type":"bulletList","content":[{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Authentication:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" disabled OIDC identities are rejected after provisioning and on WebSocket checks. Local JWTs carry a password-hash fingerprint, checked against the current active database user on every request and WebSocket authorization. The SPA uses one session context for local and OIDC accounts. "},{"type":"text","text":"/api/me","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" returns the current identity and administrator status. Configuration failures show a retry page instead of pretending first-run setup is available."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Authorization:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" document lists, hierarchical exports, versions, and derived collections respect page access. Team/project creation and moves validate the destination. Delete and grant actions require the corresponding containing-space permission. Integration credentials are usable only within their authorized scope. Theme and system operations require administration. "},{"type":"text","text":"/api/documents/{id}/capabilities","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" controls editing affordances."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Media:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" "},{"type":"text","text":"0011_image_ownership.sql","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" adds uploader ownership. Private images require an authorized owner, library, or page reader; configured site branding is public. Rendering URLs add credentials only for Kollab's media endpoints. Raster uploads validate decoded format and dimensions before allocation (40 megapixels, 10 MB); passive SVG drawing elements are allowed while scripts, external references, events, and directives are rejected. Local storage uses "},{"type":"text","text":"os.Root","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" and atomic writes to constrain paths and avoid partially written files. Macro markup uses DOMPurify; document preview frames are sandboxed."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Archive recovery:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" "},{"type":"text","text":"kollab.database.v2","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" snapshots include all public application tables, permission records, attachments, version history, and the migration ledger. Restore validates table completeness and migration checksums, then uses one PostgreSQL transaction with sequence repair. ZIP paths and expanded size are checked before installation. Staging occurs inside the uploads mount; per-entry renames preserve the mount itself. Database failure rolls files back. Failed filesystem rollback preserves its recovery directory and reports an administrator recovery requirement. Local and PostgreSQL maintenance gates exclude ordinary HTTP requests, collaboration mutations, and scheduled cleanup across replicas while exporting/restoring. Archive restoration disconnects editors with a reload signal so pre-restore CRDT state is discarded. An interrupted file operation leaves a recovery marker that fences further workspace operations. Replica invalidation commits atomically with restored database state."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Offline synchronization:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" all primary-key application tables receive tracking triggers after permission-schema initialization. Imports apply ordered upserts/deletes transactionally with outbound tracking suppressed. Packages require an HMAC SHA-256 signature using an operator-provided "},{"type":"text","text":"SYNC_SIGNING_KEY","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" of at least 32 bytes. A common key and compatible migration ledger are required between installations. The supported format is "},{"type":"text","text":"kollab.sync.v3","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":"; legacy sync packages are rejected. Per-installation vector clocks, portable permission identities, explicit conflict review, tombstones, and retained losing versions support both directions. See "},{"type":"text","text":"the synchronization design","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"/teams/07f8fd73-cdf4-516a-91ed-41cee8e97b70/p/19a0c982-2c1a-56a3-9536-556f77f40acb/docs/232d23bb-5467-54e1-bd6c-60590a284935","target":"_self","rel":"noopener noreferrer"}}]},{"type":"text","text":"."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Collaboration:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" "},{"type":"text","text":"0012_collaborative_state.sql","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" stores a bounded full Yjs state per page. "},{"type":"text","text":"0013_collaborative_projection.sql","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" adds the readable JSON committed atomically with each accepted revision. The browser derives this JSON from the same Yjs fragment, and document reads, keyword search, exports, sharing, and image-access checks prefer it over delayed REST saves. Clients send revisioned snapshots; PostgreSQL compare-and-swap rejects stale writes and returns the current state for client-side CRDT merging. Acknowledgments identify the accepted update, and changes made while an acknowledgment is outstanding are sent afterward. Reconnect merges local state with persisted state. The content editor waits for synchronization before enabling editing, avoiding duplicate CRDT initialization from a stale JSON copy. REST saves remain serialized, pending content survives component teardown, and the browser warns before leaving with a pending save. Version restoration atomically saves a recovery snapshot, restores JSON, and invalidates the prior CRDT state, then disconnects that page's clients for reload. Queued messages from detached clients are ignored. PostgreSQL polling shares accepted snapshots, presence, cursors, and restoration epochs across API replicas. Docker Compose defaults to two replicas with a shared uploads mount; the tested concurrency target is five editors."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Sharing:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" "},{"type":"text","text":"/share/{token}","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" resolves through "},{"type":"text","text":"POST /api/shared-links/open","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":", keeping the raw link token out of API request URLs. Password and expiry checks apply. Anonymous visitors can read; comment/edit actions require a signed-in identity. Authenticated API calls carry page-scoped sharing headers; WebSocket sharing credentials use a subprotocol field and are rechecked on updates/delivery. Only viewer, commenter, and editor sharing roles can be created. Public scope accepts the existing "},{"type":"text","text":"anyone","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" payload and "},{"type":"text","text":"anonymous","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" alias. Shared media uses signed one-hour page capabilities; each image/attachment request rechecks link expiry/revocation."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Integrations and exports:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" GitLab single-issue cards call the configured GitLab provider rather than returning sample issues. Issue lists traverse project/group pagination with a 30-second deadline and 100-page limit; failure is explicit rather than returning a misleading partial list. Credential-bearing redirects cannot change origin. The internal Confluence fetch service requests actual page content and metadata, but it is not wired to an operator-facing live embed flow. Confluence archive import is the available user workflow. Export excludes restricted descendants, constrains network image downloads, and reports PDF failures explicitly. The backend image includes Chromium and fonts; PDF rendering has a timeout, concurrency limit, disabled scripting, and blocked external resource requests."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Delivery:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" production startup requires a persistent database URL. Disposable automatic databases require explicit "},{"type":"text","text":"DEV_DATABASE=true","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":". Vite API and WebSocket traffic defaults to the same origin. Docker publishes the edge proxy rather than conflicting backend/proxy host ports. Frontend builds perform the actual TypeScript project build; CI runs frontend tests/lint/build and the full Go suite with >60% coverage before deployment."}]}]},{"type":"listItem","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Empty states and themes:","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" repository collection responses use empty arrays. Automatically generated team/project portal content uses JSON serialization so punctuation and control characters in names cannot corrupt its document payload. Personal settings handle empty pages, image libraries resolve abbreviated routes to persisted IDs, and load failures are visible. Preset choices persist in browser storage; saved workspace colors apply to the Default preset. Primary button foregrounds are selected for contrast and injected through "},{"type":"text","text":"--primary-contrast","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":"."}]}]}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Verification status"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The complete Go suite passed with "},{"type":"text","text":"63.9% statement coverage","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":", including disposable PostgreSQL integration tests. Collaboration, document, storage, multi-replica coordination, synchronization, and maintenance race checks passed. The frontend TypeScript project build and production bundling passed. All "},{"type":"text","text":"113 frontend tests in 25 files","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":" passed. ESLint completed with "},{"type":"text","text":"0 errors and 318 warnings","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":"; these warnings remain technical debt and are not evidence of complete production qualification. A dry-run offline "},{"type":"text","text":"npm ci","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" validated lockfile consistency."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Real-browser checks used an isolated API, Vite process, disposable PostgreSQL container, and synthetic account. Verified login/session recovery, editing and reloading, content persistence through API restart, password-protected anonymous sharing, link revocation, empty personal settings, task/notification/trash empty states, abbreviated image-library routes, and document readability in light/dark Default, Workbench, Editorial, and Neobrutal presets. These are bounded workflow checks, not a claim that every macro or external provider was exercised."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The initial entry bundle was reduced from approximately 1.3 MB gzip to 283 KB gzip by deferring editor routes. The editor itself remains large (approximately 1 MB gzip), and the build reports large-chunk warnings. Existing lint warnings remain; errors are release-blocking in CI."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Operating decisions and remaining deployment checks"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The user selected bidirectional offline synchronization, multiple API instances, and 2–5 concurrent editors. Verification uses the local computer. No old backups or legacy sync compatibility are required. These decisions are implemented in "},{"type":"text","text":"the synchronization design","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"/teams/07f8fd73-cdf4-516a-91ed-41cee8e97b70/p/19a0c982-2c1a-56a3-9536-556f77f40acb/docs/232d23bb-5467-54e1-bd6c-60590a284935","target":"_self","rel":"noopener noreferrer"}}]},{"type":"text","text":"."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The additional integration tests cover two installations exchanging updates and permissions, reviewed conflicts and reverse propagation, deletion tombstones, compact replication cursors, destination-only dependent records, two hubs with five editors, replica recovery, shared media credentials, distributed maintenance, and retained file versions. Frontend tests cover the conflict review flow and editor initialization/restore fencing. Two actual API processes started concurrently against an isolated database, and browser edits were observed in both directions through separate API endpoints. The Caddy configuration passed offline adaptation validation."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Real OIDC, GitLab, Confluence, AI/embedding, document conversion, and TLS deployment configuration still need qualification with the intended services and credentials. No production deployment or live provider mutation was requested. Azure backup and Jira remain excluded prototypes. Existing lint warnings and large editor chunks are recorded technical debt, not hidden by the passing checks."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"No deployment, production data migration, or provider-side mutation was performed. The disposable verification processes, database container, and browser tabs were cleaned up after checks. Vector embeddings and derived task/property indexes are still refreshed through the normal save pipeline; keyword search and direct content reads use the durable projection. Version restore should be performed after editors save their work. All API replicas coordinate the operation and invalidate stale editor state."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Documentation reconciliation"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The user-guide index lists all user/admin pages. Deployment, complete archives, signed bidirectional sync, replica coordination, provider availability, template creation, private media, sharing, and restored-editor reload instructions are aligned with current routes and implementation. In-app "},{"type":"text","text":"HelpAdmin","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" and "},{"type":"text","text":"HelpVersions","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" present the same operational behavior; the admin-help back action returns to settings. Documentation links use repository-relative paths instead of one developer's machine paths. Azure backup and Jira stay explicitly marked as prototypes; internal provider helper code is not presented as a complete UI feature."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Source: design/production_readiness.md"}]}]}

The API verifies the token's issuer, signature, expiry, configured API audience, and delegated API scope. Do not use a client secret in the browser or configure a generic shared JWT secret for OIDC."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"After the first administrator has logged in and other administrators are configured, remove "},{"type":"text","text":"BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USER_ID","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" from the deployment configuration.
